# spectral.absorption { #clerq.spectral.absorption }

```python
spectral.absorption(solver, field_idx, z_idx=-1, *, window=None)
```

Field absorption in the frequency domain.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type              | Description                                             | Default    |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| solver    | PropagationSolver | A PropagationSolver object.                             | _required_ |
| field_idx | int               | Field to return spectrum of.                            | _required_ |
| z_idx     | int               | z step at which to return absorption.                   | `-1`       |
| window    | str \| None       | Optional SciPy window name passed to :func:`rabi_freq`. | `None`     |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type       | Description                                  |
|--------|------------|----------------------------------------------|
|        | np.ndarray | Array[num_freq_points] of absorption values. |

## Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

In the linear regime this is the imaginary part of the linear
susceptibility (with a factor k/2).
See TP Ogden thesis Eqn (2.58)
